solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A cat that's very small

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Someone describes a kitten or toy cat as tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle is the classic example of something minute, the smallest unit of an element.

clue.text: Scarcity beginning to destroy planet

indicators.note: the beginning of the word destroy is its opening letter only

parts.note: Earth is our planet

explanation.surface: A shortage of resources is starting to wreck the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both mean a shortage or lack of something.

clue.text: Cheap yet fancy part of pirate costume

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means imagine, so the letters of cheap yet are freely reimagined

explanation.surface: A dressing-up item for a pirate outfit that is inexpensive but showy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like an adjective describing the costume, but it signals rearranging CHEAPYET.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a patch over one eye is a stock item of pirate fancy dress.

clue.text: Foreign money turned up in hideout

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the rial is the currency of Iran and other countries

explanation.surface: Smuggled foreign cash was found in a criminal hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a den or retreat where an animal or fugitive hides.

clue.text: One cold summer in Paris with a refreshing drink

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps
ete is the French word for summer

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a chilled drink on a hot summer day in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: chilled tea is a cooling beverage for warm weather.

clue.text: English poet's always following popular mastermind

indicators.note: following means the poetic word comes after the word for popular

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A writer notes that a constant English poet comes after a popular plotter.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in E'ER is dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms as verbs: to plan and contrive a scheme cleverly.

clue.text: Determined swimmer trapped in filthy place

indicators.note: being trapped in puts the fish inside the dirty place

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, a byword for a dirty place
an eel is a fish, so a swimmer

explanation.surface: A resolute fish is stuck in a squalid spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: resolute and unwavering, with a will of iron.

clue.text: Get high when clubs close

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
a close is an end or finish

explanation.surface: People take drugs as the nightclubs shut.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal sense: to rise or climb upwards, reaching a greater height.

clue.text: Indecent one causing trouble with cowboy?

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous troublemaker
a roper is a cowboy who lassos cattle

explanation.surface: A rude troublemaker is linked with a cowboy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: unseemly or offending against decency.

clue.text: Follow story on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than read, so the word for story is sounded

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep up with a serial broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to shadow or trail someone secretly.

clue.text: Fashionable comic blockbuster

parts.note: a wit is a funny person, a comic
a blockbuster is a hit film or book

explanation.surface: A trendy comedy film that is a huge success.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: up to date and trendy in style or attitudes.

clue.text: Inexperienced person elected, with no change in Washington DC

parts.note: in means elected, as of a party in power
a cent is a small coin in American money

explanation.surface: A newly elected novice arrives in Washington with no reforms.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a naive person, unworldly and lacking experience.

clue.text: Large mammal in western sound

parts.note: sound means healthy, as does hale

explanation.surface: A big animal lives in the waters of a western inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a body of water or a noise, but means healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the blue one is the largest animal ever known.

clue.text: Flora and fauna in large rocky field beyond Wisconsin

indicators.note: beyond means the other pieces follow the state abbreviation

parts.note: WI is the postal abbreviation for Wisconsin
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

indicators.note: rocky means unstable, so the letters of field are shaken up

explanation.surface: Plants and animals thrive in a big stony meadow past Wisconsin.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: the plants and animals of a region, living in the wild.

clue.text: Charlie greeting Greek character

parts.note: C is Charlie in the radio alphabet
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: Someone named Charlie says hello to a Greek person.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the twenty-second letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Hymn composed about quiet spirit of nature

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the quiet letter
composed means put together anew, so the letters of hymn are rearranged

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: A hymn was written about a quiet nature spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' looks musical but turns HYMN into NYMH, which goes 'about' P.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythology: a minor female deity of woods, rivers or mountains.

clue.text: Man bored by R&B and hard rock

indicators.note: bored by means pierced by, so the music letters go inside

parts.note: male means a man
R and B are the letters of the abbreviation for rhythm and blues

explanation.surface: A man is tired of rhythm and blues and heavy rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bored' means drilled through, not tired; 'hard rock' is not music.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a metamorphic limestone stone used in sculpture and building.

clue.text: Length is originally extremely uniform

indicators.note: originally means only the start of the word is is used

parts.note: very means extremely

explanation.surface: A remark that a length of something is basically very even.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' looks like an adjective, but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a distinctive outfit worn by servants or staff of a company.

clue.text: Group of characters very eagerly at first entering parliament

indicators.note: entering means that letter goes inside the birds

parts.note: a parliament is the collective noun for owls

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of eagerly

explanation.surface: A party of people keenly enters parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'parliament' of owls is their collective noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: A, E, I, O and U form a set of letters of the alphabet.

clue.text: Cliff and Mark left after surgery

definitions.meaning: a crag or steep rocky outcrop
a healed wound's lasting trace on the skin

explanation.surface: Two men, Cliff and Mark, leave hospital after an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a steep rock face, and a mark from a healed wound.

clue.text: State law cutting expensive drug

indicators.note: cutting means the legal word slices into the costly one

parts.note: dear means costly
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A government law cuts back on a costly drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb but is the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the first state to ratify the US Constitution.

clue.text: Odd wild duck that couldn't fly

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of odd are scrambled

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A strange wild duck that was flightless.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the extinct flightless bird of Mauritius.

clue.text: Cover page missing from preliminary version of document

indicators.note: missing means the page letter is absent from the trial print

parts.note: a proof is a trial printing for checking

explanation.surface: A cover page is absent from a draft document.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: the top covering of a building.

clue.text: Article in French about young man exposing everything

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
c is the abbreviation for circa, about
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A French piece of writing about a young man showing all.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: naked, wearing no clothes at all.

clue.text: Short trip to study bird of prey

indicators.note: short means the word is cut back by its last letter

parts.note: to trip is to fall
con means to study closely

explanation.surface: A brief outing to observe a hunting bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a fast hawk-like raptor, such as the peregrine.
